Subject: Capacity harmonization for Lumina Health — buffer pool smoothing proposal

Hi Sarah,

Quick follow from our call last week — thanks again for walking us through the expected product ramp. We pulled April usage and saw the expected spike pattern repeated across night batches and morning inference peaks. I attached a CSV with hourly GPU-hours (lumina_usage_apr2027.csv).

Recommendation (short term): add a modest dedicated buffer pool of 60 GPUs for a 12-week ramp window, paired with a temporary smoothing policy that amortizes 25% of those GPUs against a short-term commit. That lets you handle the Q3 burst without immediately moving to a larger multi-tranche commit.

What this changes operationally:
- Predictable baseline capacity for prefetch/eviction-sensitive workloads (reduces cold-kv misses)
- Autoscaling still active for sudden spikes; buffer pool absorbs sustained delta to avoid cold-start token tax
- We propose a one-time SOW amendment (proposed_adjustment_SOW.pdf) and a 90-day review to align final commit size to realized utilization.

Can you confirm budget appetite and procurement timeline? If useful, Marissa and I can send a line-item breakdown for PO. Dev mapped a minimal config that preserves your 99th percentile latency — copying him for any technical constraints.

Thanks,
Priyom

Sarah — quick technical note to supplement the SOW:

The buffer pool approach behaves differently from autoscaling in three ways we want you to be aware of:
1) KV-cache warmness: dedicated buffer GPUs will keep short-lived KV caches warm for recurring prompt patterns; this reduces per-request token cost by ~8-12% versus cold starts in our tests.
2) Latency SLO: we can guarantee your 99th percentile latency stays within current SLA when the buffer pool is sized at >=60 for your peak cohort, provided sequence length distribution remains within the April profile.
3) Fallbacks: if the buffer pool fills and demand continues to rise, autoscaling will still add ephemeral instances. Those ephemeral instances have higher marginal cost and slightly higher 99th pct latency under double-peaks — the smoothing policy is intended to minimize that scenario.

Operational requests: please confirm whether you need region pinning (we recommend us-west for lower egress and data locality) and whether you want the 90-day utilization review to use the conservative or aggressive threshold in the SOW appendix.

Technical contact if you want to run a quick two-week canary: dev.patel@redwood.com
